# Premium upgrade modal

The modal follows the supplied “Mailloop – Upgrade modal pp.html” reference.
Only the comparison body scrolls. The header, feature chip, checkout action,
dismiss action, and pricing link remain visible. Premium appears first below
700px. Both cards reuse the existing `CardSpotlight` cursor tracking; their glow,
theme transitions, and button shine respect reduced motion.

## Audit and theme decisions

The previous modal used a native dialog and shared the public pricing cards.
The repo had no shadcn Dialog primitive or Radix Dialog dependency. The approved
implementation adds `@radix-ui/react-dialog` and a local shadcn-style primitive,
while leaving public pricing cards unchanged.

The modal reuses the existing font mappings, `--ring` for keyboard focus,
`--plan-card-spotlight` for the subtle cursor glow, and `--on-accent` for the
existing semantic backdrop treatment. The approved palette
choice uses dedicated modal colors rather than substituting the app's different
background, card, foreground, muted, and border values.

`src/app/theme-tokens.css` defines `--upgrade-app`, `--upgrade-surface`,
`--upgrade-surface2`, `--upgrade-text`, `--upgrade-muted`, `--upgrade-border`,
`--upgrade-grad`, `--upgrade-btn-fg`, `--upgrade-glow`, `--upgrade-ok`,
`--upgrade-okbg`, `--upgrade-dot`, `--upgrade-shine`, `--upgrade-check`, and the
checkmark mask. The selectors are, in cascade order:

1. `:root` (Lavender)
2. `html[data-theme="dark"]` (Nightbloom)
3. `html[data-theme="light"][data-appearance="vercel"]` (Chalk)
4. `html[data-theme="dark"][data-appearance="vercel"]` (Obsidian)

Only changed variables are overridden. `globals.css` maps colors and shadows
through `@theme inline`, and provides the gradient utility and scoped decorative
rules. No theme-switching or storage code was added.

The supplied purple gradients failed AA with white button text. Lavender uses
`#6f4ac5 → #9a45b3`; Nightbloom uses `#765ccc → #a54dbe`. Nightbloom's smaller
darkening also preserves contrast for the large gradient stat numbers on their
dark tiles. The shine stays at the button edges to preserve label contrast.
Prices continue using the caller's localized value, including ₹299 for India.

## Opening with feature context

Inside the existing provider:

```tsx
const openUpgrade = usePremiumUpgrade();
openUpgrade({ feature: "roles", trigger: event.currentTarget });
```

| Key              | Existing entry point / highlighted row                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `roles`          | Compose role control and Premium role lock / recipient role editing                         |
| `reminders`      | Reminder settings controls and Save / follow-up reminders                                   |
| `replied`        | History Mark replied / reply tracking                                                       |
| `csv`            | Contacts CSV import / CSV import                                                            |
| `templates`      | Extra or retained template editor, template locks, Compose picker / templates and shortcuts |
| `shortlist`      | History shortlist actions / History shortcut                                                |
| `themes`         | Locked Chalk/Obsidian options, including appearance-menu fallback / all four themes         |
| `role-shortcuts` | Outreach preferences at the Free shortcut limit / templates and shortcuts                   |
| `highlights`     | Locked preview color / preview highlight colors                                             |
| `repeat`         | Existing repeat-send gates / manual repeat sends                                            |

`trigger` is optional; the provider captures the active element when omitted.
`openUpgrade()` displays the roles chip with no highlighted row. An explicit key
highlights exactly one row. The direct component also accepts
`<PremiumUpgradeDialog feature="roles" onClose={close} />`.

Shared `FeatureLock` and `PremiumLock` components accept `upgradeFeature`
separately from their descriptive `feature` label. Existing allowance reasons,
details, gating, and fallback actions are retained. The checkout handler is
unchanged; this change does not alter billing or checkout behavior.

## Files changed by this redesign

- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
- `src/app/theme-tokens.css`, `src/app/globals.css`
- `src/components/ui/dialog.tsx`
- `src/components/premium-upgrade-dialog.tsx`, `premium-upgrade-provider.tsx`
- `src/components/feature-lock.tsx`, `premium-lock.tsx`
- `src/components/compose.tsx`, `forms.tsx`, `appearance-control.tsx`, `preview-highlight.tsx`
- `src/components/contacts/ImportContacts.tsx`, `ContactShortlistAction.tsx`
- `src/components/history/RowActions.tsx`
- `src/components/settings/FollowUpReminders.tsx`, `OutreachPreferences.tsx`
- `src/app/(app)/templates/page.tsx`
- `tests/browser/premium-upgrade.spec.ts`, `feature-gates.spec.ts`, `appearance.spec.ts`
- `docs/upgrade-modal.md`

Existing screenshot references remain unchanged. Browser tests use disposable
databases and fake provider credentials through `scripts/test-usage-db.ts`.

## Verification

- TypeScript, ESLint, color-literal checks, formatting, and production build passed.
- All 418 runnable unit tests passed; database-only tests retain their existing skips.
- 35 distinct focused browser cases passed across the final run and targeted reruns.
  Five duplicate mobile cases are intentionally skipped because those tests own
  their viewport/theme matrices. The two initial light-theme failures came from
  the new contrast helper not expanding shorthand hex; both passed after fixing
  the helper. No visual baseline was updated.
- Coverage includes all four palettes, 320/360/390px widths, the 699/700px breakpoint,
  fixed header/footer, access to the last feature, focus containment/restoration,
  live changes through the existing switcher, cursor spotlight, reduced motion,
  feature contexts, localized pricing, and unchanged checkout retry requests.
- The embedded `startCheckout` handler was compared with its original source and
  remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Shared public card design (2026-11-04)

The modal and public pricing now share `pricing/plan-card.tsx`, including the
compact features, context metadata, configuration-derived stats, texture, border,
and cursor glow. The modal still owns its scrolling body and fixed checkout
footer. The public `PricingCards` wrapper adds bottom-aligned caller actions and
uses “Free plan” unless the signed-in user's current plan is Free. Premium's
badge also identifies the current plan when applicable. This supersedes the
historical note above that public cards were left unchanged.
